item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mixed, leaning negative. Tshisekedi did appoint several clearly professional figures in 2024, especially in finance and planning, and he publicly backed oversight bodies. But the cabinet was delayed by internal bargaining, the final lineup still reflected coalition/job jostling, and some key posts went to close allies rather than depoliticized outsiders.

**Accepted Claims**
- [DR Congo president appoints country's first female prime minister](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-president-appoints-countrys-first-female-prime-minister-2024-04-01/) | Reuters | 2024-04-01 | Tshisekedi appointed Judith Suminwa, then planning minister, as prime minister. That is real evidence of competence-based staffing at the top of government. | IDs: 7B.5, 7B.3
- [Madame Judith SUMINWA TULUKA, nommée Première Ministre de la République Démocratique du Congo](https://communication.gouv.cd/actualites/communications-du-gouvernement/18/madame-judith-suminwa-tuluka-nommee-premiere-ministre-de-la-republique-democratique-du-congo) | Ministère de la Communication et Médias | 2024-04-01 | The presidency said Suminwa was chosen for her skills and development-planning experience. This is self-reported, but it supports the reading that the PM pick was technocratic rather than purely loyalist. | IDs: 7B.5, 7B.3
- [RDC : Fwamba Likunde, un technocrate rompu à la tête du ministère des Finances](https://acp.cd/economie/rdc-fwamba-likunde-un-technocrate-rompu-a-la-tete-du-ministere-des-finances-par-elysee-kakese/) | ACP | 2024-05-30 | ACP described Doudou Fwamba as an experienced finance technocrat with public-finance expertise. This is direct positive evidence that Tshisekedi placed a competent professional in a strategic portfolio. | IDs: 7B.5, 7B.3
- [Doudou Fwamba: The new face of Finance in the DRC](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/drc-names-new-government-after-months-of-delay-46846207/) | Reuters | 2024-05-29 | Reuters reported the new finance minister had a technical background and ministry experience. That supports a professional staffing reading for a key economic post. | IDs: 7B.5, 7B.3
- [DR Congo names new government after months of delay](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-names-new-government-after-months-of-delay-46846207/) | Reuters | 2024-05-29 | Internal jostling for jobs delayed cabinet formation for months, and the final cabinet remained larger than expected despite pressure to cut costs. This points to coalition bargaining and patronage pressures, not a clean merit-only cabinet. | IDs: 7B.5, 7B.4, 7B.3
- [DRC parliament elects speaker in delayed vote days after foiled coup](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2024/05/23/drc-parliament-elects-speaker-in-delayed-vote-days-after-foiled-coup) | Reuters | 2024-05-23 | Vital Kamerhe, a close ally of Tshisekedi and former chief of staff, became speaker. Because he is a loyal political heavyweight rather than a neutral technocrat, this is evidence of ally placement to consolidate power. | IDs: 7B.5, 7B.4
- [Le Chef de l’État a assisté à l’ouverture de la session extraordinaire du conseil supérieur de la Cour des comptes](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_chef_de_l_etat_a_assiste_a_louverture_de_la_session_extraordinaire_du_conseil_superieur_de_la_cour_des_comptes) | Présidence RDC | 2024-10-07 | The Court of Accounts publicly credited Tshisekedi’s support for anti-corruption control and public-finance oversight. This is positive evidence that he backed at least one professional accountability institution. | IDs: 7B.5, 7B.4
- [Congolese president sacks military top brass in major reshuffle](https://theprint.in/world/congolese-president-sacks-military-top-brass-in-major-reshuffle/2411531/) | Reuters | 2024-12-20 | Tshisekedi replaced the armed forces chief, military intelligence head, and many senior officers, and Reuters noted earlier reforms were framed as efficiency-boosting. This is mixed evidence: it can be read as corrective professionalization, but also as politically managed elite reshuffling. | IDs: 7B.5, 7B.4
- [Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts-report](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-2024-01-15/) | Reuters | 2024-01-15 | CENI failed to account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement. That is negative evidence that a key state body under Tshisekedi’s broader system was not being managed in a clean, professionally controlled way. | IDs: 7B.5, 7B.4, 7B.3

**Search Gap**
- I did not find strong 2024 reporting tying Tshisekedi’s immediate family to explicit appointments, donor patronage, or named business associates in government.
- I also did not find solid evidence of an openly nepotistic cabinet built around relatives. The stronger pattern is coalition patronage, loyal allies, and a mix of technocrats plus power-preserving appointments.
- So the best-supported conclusion is not “family capture proven,” but “some real technocratic appointments, offset by significant ally/coalition patronage and weak institutional discipline.”
